moat_against: Cyclical — conservative owner's earnings were negative in FY2022 and FY2023
Aerospace and defense concentration; tied to OEM build rates and defense budgets
Capital-intensive — FY2026 capex $242.7M vs D&A $147.1M, plus brownfield execution risk
Raw-material (nickel, titanium, cobalt) price volatility and capable rivals such as ATI
moat_for: Qualification/certification barriers — alloys certified per jet engine and airframe program, re-qualification takes years
Proven pricing power — record SAO operating margin and a long run of consecutive margin expansion
Scarce high-purity melt capacity, being added to by the brownfield expansion
Long OEM relationships in aerospace and defense with multi-year order visibility
moat_justification: Moderate moat (6/10): real qualification and certification barriers in aerospace alloys — alloys are certified per engine/airframe program and re-qualifying a supplier takes years — plus scarce high-purity melt capacity and proven pricing power (record SAO margin, long run of margin expansion). But it is not wide: owner's earnings were negative in FY2022 and FY2023, so returns were not held through the cycle; the business is capital-intensive, aerospace/defense-concentrated, and exposed to raw-material prices and OEM build rates.
name: Carpenter Technology Corporation
one_liner: Good cyclical alloy franchise, moat 6/10, at a scarcity price — weighted IRR 5.08% and weighted IV@15% $68.83 vs price $380.56; every scenario, including super bull, is Tier D, and it clears 15% only at about $68.83.
